roles.title: Commandant of the Marine Corps
roles.source_excerpt: General Eric M. Smith Commandant of the Marine Corps

web.named_query: ("Eric M. Smith" OR "Douglas A. Schiess") AI artificial intelligence superintelligence policy statements

summary.text: In April 2024, Eric M. Smith said the Marine Corps was aggressively leveraging AI, robotics, and commercial technology as part of the Department of Defense’s Replicator Initiative, and he described Replicator as an opportunity to accelerate modernization. In May 2025 statements, Smith described integrating AI with advanced sensors, targeting systems, and edge-based capabilities to improve sensing, precision fires, and electronic warfare. In a May 2026 statement, Smith said Dynamis enables AI-powered decision advantage and that MSS, used by over 4,900 Marines, reflects a commitment to leveraging AI at all echelons and improving joint kill chain capabilities. Smith also said the Marine Corps would not reorganize based on AI but would use available tools, and he cited AI/ML for retention and talent management and AI-driven adaptive learning in education.

None supports an ai_overall label; this conclusion is limited to the supplied evidence.

statements.text: The Marine Corps is actively engaged, participating, and, in some instances, leading efforts within the Department of Defense’s Replicator Initiative, which aims to field attritable autonomous systems at scale and in multiple domains. To accomplish this task, the Marine Corps is aggressively leveraging AI, robotics, and commercial technology.
